1965.notes: Left out: grain scale and noise settings (octave/algorithm-like), the blend opacities, and the normal-map strength, which the common controls cover. Pattern choice is limited to bonds that suit a plank floor.

1966.notes: Left out the texture noise controls (wavelet and fbm noise, blur, rotate). They only drive the fine vinyl grain and the bump map, so they don't make a clear visible difference. Also left out the blend opacity of the vinyl texture overlay, because it is only a faint grain.

1967.notes: Left out the vinyl texture controls (the fine wavelet and fbm noise, the embossed highlight blend) because they are fine grain and the common Bumps, Roughness and Height controls already cover them. Left out stripe thickness because the triangle widths and heights feed a math node whose effect on the line width I cannot trace reliably.

1968.notes: Only three controls are worth adding. Wallpaper Color, Stripe Color and Stripe Width are the visible parts of this material. I left out the stripe spacing, because it comes from several chained translate nodes that would have to move together. I also left out the vinyl grain and emboss, because the fine noise only feeds the height and a faint overlay, and the normal strength is excluded.

1969.notes: Controls cover the grass colors that reach the base color, the light and dark patch amounts, and the patch size. I left out the blade-pattern noise (fbm4, voronoi, blur, UV remapper) because it only drives fine blade structure and its settings are noise internals. I left out the base green (uniform_2) to stay within a short list; it is mostly covered by the gradient and the Hue control.

1970.notes: Only the paint color, the trowel marks and their density are worth exposing. Most of the graph is grayscale noise feeding the normal map, so I left it out. I also left out the fine speckle noise, because it is quality-level detail and not an obvious artist control.

1971.notes: Colors and checker size are the main changes. The graph's other noise/slope-blur branch ends in colorize_5, which I could not trace to the base color, so I left it alone. The pattern wave types and the Xor combiner are not exposed.

1972.notes: Only two controls beyond the common ones. Most of the graph builds the brush-stroke relief that feeds the normal map. Its blends and mask thresholds are tangled and hard to trace to a clear visible change. Sliders on them would mostly duplicate Bumps. I left out controls on the grey colorize and the noise-over-paint blend because it is unclear which output channel they drive.

1973.notes: Only the trim color and its tint strength are exposed. The grooves come from a tiler whose translate nodes are fixed offsets tied to the 12 rows, so a row-count control would misalign them. I also left out groove width because its effect is hard to trace through the blur and normal-map chain. The gray colorize gradients feed roughness and relief, so they are not color controls.

1974.notes: Controls cover the plaster base color, the dark stains and light patches that reach the albedo, and the size of the mottling. colorize and colorize_3 only feed the normal map and a greyscale channel, so I left their gradients out. Seeds, blend modes and noise settings are excluded as per the rules. The blend opacities are assumed to mask the two overlay layers; their exact blend order is untraced.

1976.notes: Only the brown colors were traced through to the base color. The gray stone colors (uniform_10, uniform_11) sit behind a very narrow mask and don't show in the preview, so they got no control. I also skipped the warp, distort and tiler randomness values, which would only change fine variation.

1977.notes: Controls cover tile layout, grout width, tile pattern, the strength of the mottled surface blend and its size. I left out the Colorize gradients (7 stops on the main one, dark grey tones only) and all noise algorithm or octave settings. Roughness and height are covered by the common controls. The outputs of blend2_2, blend2_3 and colorize_5 were hard to trace, so I did not expose their blends.

1979.notes: Controls cover panel and tile layout, gap widths and the tint layer. I left out the two 7- and 8-stop colorize gradients (colorize_3 and colorize_4): they are random per-tile greys mapped to many stops, so the stops are not separate parts a user would pick. I also left out the bevel and round values because they are 0 and their effect is hard to trace. Wear and dirt come from noise blends with fixed opacity, so there is no clean amount control.

1980.notes: Left out: per-brick color variation (the Blend opacity after Fill to random gray), because it is not clear which input is which, so its effect is hard to trace. Also left out: noise scales and Slope blur, which are texture internals, and bevel and corner roundness, whose effect is subtle on this wall.

1981.notes: Left out the Offset and Corner/Round parameters because they would overlap with Layout and are hard to read on a tile this fine. The speckle noise and the roughness mask (colorize_5) are left out since they only add fine detail. Gap Width on the normal-map path was skipped as redundant with Grout Width.

1983.notes: The base color comes from colorize_2, a noisy gradient with about 100 stops, so it has no 2 to 4 stop meaning and I did not make a gradient or color control for it. The other two colorize nodes (the brown and gray ones) have no link to the output. I left out a moss amount control because the opacity of the blends that mix moss into the slabs is not clearly traceable to the moss alone, and the common Hue and Saturation controls already shift the green. The controls below cover the layout and shape of the concrete slabs.

1984.notes: Controls cover the brick layout, mortar, bevel and brick color. I left out a mortar color control because I couldn't confidently trace which gradient (colorize_6, colorize_7 or colorize_9) is the mortar in the final blend. I left out the dirt and noise layers because they have no clear amount parameter that reaches the base color.

1985.notes: Controls cover the stone color, the stone layout, the gap width and the roundness. Left out: the speckle and moss-like tint variation (alter_hsv_2 and its noise mask), because it is subtle and only fine-tunes the stone colors. Also left out: bevel and corner, which overlap with roundness. The colorize_4 gradient is a dead end that never reaches the output, so it is not used.

1986.notes: Left out the noise settings (fbm4 scale) and blur because they are noise internals. Stripe color is a gradient control reaching the base color. Tiler offset and scale are random variation so they are exposed only as stripe irregularity.

1988.notes: The wood color comes from the first Colorize, which goes through Warp to the albedo, so I exposed its stops as color controls instead of one 5-stop gradient. I left out the Blend with white noise, because I could not trace where it ends up (likely roughness or AO). I also left out the Epsilon of Warp and the normal map settings, since they are technical or already covered by Bumps.

1989.notes: Only colorize_2 reaches the base color, so skin tone is a gradient control. The pore controls act on the voronoi and the blend feeding it; the blend's opacity parameter is named amount#. I left out the normal-map colorize (grey relief only) and the uniform node, which has no visible link to the output. I also left out the fbm4 warp scale, since it is a noise setting with no clear visual result.

1991.notes: Only the colorize_2 gradient is clearly the visible base color, so the controls are its three colors. I left out the other colorize nodes (they look like roughness, metallic and normal-map feeds, which the common controls already cover). I also left out the noise scale (it duplicates the common Scale) and the noise folds, iterations and persistence (noise settings).

1994.notes: Left out the width of the mortar gaps because it is set by gradient stop positions, which a control can't change. Also left out the dirt and wear opacity, since the Blend nodes mix several layers and a single opacity can't be traced to one visible effect. The 5-stop stone gradient is covered by a single stone color control instead of a gradient control.

1995.notes: The graph is a height map of a single beveled panel (polygon shapes with warped noise) that feeds the base color and the normal map. I kept only the controls I could trace to the output: the concrete tones and the panel edge softness. I left out the blend opacity, the noise scales of the warp and fbm nodes, and the gradient thresholds that build the height map. Their effects are hard to read and they mostly duplicate the common Scale and Bumps controls.
